references.authors: Torii, M.; Okita, Y.; Motohashi, K.; Sakuda, A.; Hayashi, A.
references.title: First-Principles Investigation of Mechanical Properties and Anisotropy of Argyrodite Li6PS5Cl Crystal Electrolytes
references.key_content: Li6PS5Cl DFT-D3 (VASP/PBE-D3, PAW, 500eV, 3x3x3 k-pts). Elastic: C11=47.4, C12=28.4, C44=10.4, E=27.4, B=34.7, G=10.0 GPa. Pugh ratio B/G=3.46 (ductile). Anisotropy index A=1.09 (nearly isotropic). Stress-strain: elastic region up to 20% uniaxial strain. Shear fracture at 0.7% strain → brittle under shear. {111} plane most susceptible to fracture (layered gaps). Cl movement toward Li forms Li4Cl units under shear. Bader: Li(+0.87), P(+1.32), S1(-0.99), S2(-1.69), Cl(-0.69). Particle micro-compression: strength ~76 MPa (comparable to calculated shear strength).
references.comparison_to_our_work: Their DFT-D3 E=27.4 vs our 600K snapshot E=29.1 → close agreement despite different methods. Their C44=10.4 vs our DFT 0K C44=37.9 → difference is Li ordering, not D3. Their Bader Li(+0.87) matches our v2(+0.877). Key difference: single composition vs our 6 compositions + composition-dependent trends.

references.authors: Ransom, B.; Ramdas, A.; Lomeli, E.; Fidawi, J.; Sendek, A.; Devereaux, T.; Reed, E. J.; Schindler, P.
references.title: Electrolyte Coatings for High Adhesion Interfaces in Solid-State Batteries from First Principles
references.key_content: Adhesion parameter from single-material slab cleavage energies (NOT direct interface calc). Screened 19,481 Li compounds for coatings. Uses surface energy γ_e, γ_c, γ_ec and contact angle θ to derive adhesion parameter. Key equation: γ_e = γ_ec + γ_c cos θ. Good adhesion: max(γ_e) - min(γ_c) ≤ 0. Applied to LLXO, LPS, LBS electrolyte systems.

SI_critical_points.direct_interface_validation: Table S1: Benchmarked 10 interfaces (6 electrolyte/coating + 4 Li/coating) against direct DFT interface. Quote: 'Due to artifacts from creating interfaces with small area slabs, we report the interfaces which were able to reach convergence in under 1 month of computing.'
SI_critical_points.performance: Table S2: Confusion matrix — Precision 100% (5/5 good materials correctly flagged), Recall 55.6% (missed 4/9 good materials). Method is ~10^3 faster than direct interface.
SI_critical_points.infeasibility_quote: Conclusion: 'time-consuming computational ionic relaxations of numerous surface terminations makes the determination of interfacial energies infeasible even for a small number of systems.'
SI_critical_points.equations: γ_ec = (E_ec_slab - n_e*E_e_bulk - n_c*E_c_bulk) / (2*SA_ec); E_int = 2*(γ_ec - γ_e - γ_c)

references.relevance_to_our_work: Their approach avoids interface construction entirely (surface energies only). We use direct interface with MLIP to overcome their stated infeasibility. Their 10 validation interfaces took 'under 1 month' each → we do 100 seeds × 5 comps = 500 interfaces with MLIP. Their method recall=55.6% (misses half of good materials), precision=100% (screening tool). Our method captures within-family Br trends that their approach misses (our γ_SE data shows comp1>comp2>comp3>comp4>comp5 which by their inverse rule predicts wrong within-family Wad ordering).
references.what_to_show_advisor: SI Section 'Interfacial Energy Calculations and Adhesion Parameter Benchmarking' (p. S-4 to S-5): (1) Table S1 showing only 10 validated direct interfaces, (2) 1-month convergence time per interface, (3) Table S2 confusion matrix with 55.6% recall. Main text Conclusion (p. 44400): 'infeasible even for a small number of systems' — this is exactly what our MLIP approach overcomes.

references.authors: Choi, J. M.; Kim, J.; Lee, J.-H.; Son, W.-J.; Han, S.
references.title: Atomistic Insights into Cu/Amorphous-TaxN Interfacial Adhesion via Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials: Effects of Stoichiometry and Interface Construction
references.key_content: MLIP-based direct interface adhesion study for Cu/a-TaxN (x=1,2,4). Uses SevenNet (NequIP E(3)-equivariant GNN) trained on 7984 DFT structures (RMSE 4.5 meV/atom, 0.3 eV/A force). Three interface construction methods: relaxed (static), annealed (1000K 1ns), deposited (Cu deposition 7.7ns). SMD (steered molecular dynamics) with Jarzynski equality to compute Wad. Examined stoichiometry effect (Ta/N=1,2,4).

detailed_methods.DFT: VASP, PBE, 450 eV cutoff, 2x2x2 k-grid for ~10Å cells, 1e-6 eV convergence
detailed_methods.MLIP_training: SevenNet package, NequIP architecture, channel=32, layers=3, lmax=3, cutoff=5.5Å

interface_construction.deposited: 3100 Cu atoms deposited on a-TaxN slab, 7.7 ns total

detailed_methods.SMD: Spring constant k=0.01 eV/Å²/atom, pulling velocity v=0.01 Å/ps, 3 independent SMD per condition (configs sampled every 100 ps during 300K equilibration)
detailed_methods.Wad_calculation: Wad = final plateau of U_PMF from Jarzynski equality

references.relevance_to_our_work: MOST SIMILAR published paper. Both use MLIP + direct interface + multiple construction methods + composition effect. Key differences: (1) they use SMD (force-based, Jarzynski), we use separation (energy-based); (2) they vary stoichiometry, we vary Br substitution; (3) their system Cu/TaN (semiconductor), ours SE/NCM (battery); (4) they train their own MLIP (SevenNet), we use UMA/MACE off-the-shelf.
references.what_to_show_advisor: Section 2 METHODS (pages 11167-11169) — shows EXACTLY how detailed MLIP adhesion methods should be. Particularly: (1) Section 2.1 Training Set (detailed DFT params + MQA protocol), (2) Section 2.2 MLIP Training (SevenNet config, RMSE), (3) Section 2.3 Interface Construction (3 methods with specific protocols), (4) Section 2.4 SMD (spring k, velocity, Jarzynski). Methods span FULL 3 pages! This justifies our ~25-line methods as actually CONCISE compared to published standard.
references.supports_our_methodology: Published Dec 2025 in respected ACS journal. Korean group (SNU Seungwu Han). Validates: (1) MLIP direct interface is standard modern approach, (2) multiple interface construction methods is expected practice, (3) methods section of 2-3 pages is normal for MLIP adhesion papers. Our methods section is comparable or even shorter.

references.authors: Xiong, L.; Wen, P.; Zhang, Y.; Liu, X.; Ning, J.; Wang, X.; Wang, H.; Yang, Z.
references.title: Exploring efficient solid electrolyte based on Nd doped BaSnF4 for fluoride-ion batteries at atomic scale
references.key_content: First-principles DFT study of Nd-doped BaSnF4 (Ba(1-x)Nd(x)SnF(4+x), x=0, 0.02, 0.0625, 0.125, 0.25) for fluoride-ion battery solid electrolyte. Optimal composition Ba0.875Nd0.125SnF4.125 shows F-ion conductivity 5.35e-3 S/cm at 300K (vs BaSnF4 3.50e-4 S/cm = 15× enhancement). F-ion diffusion barrier reduced 0.71→0.18 eV via Nd-induced Ba-F coordination distortion. Heterovalent Nd3+→Ba2+ substitution with charge-compensating interstitial F- (auto-balance). B/G ratio 1.82→1.97 → improved ductility (Pugh criterion). Wide electrochemical window (4.86-5.66 V vs Ba, 6.38-7.57 V vs Nd). Excellent thermal stability (-120°C to 120°C, AIMD verified).
references.system: BaSnF4 (P4/nmm tetragonal, layered Ba-Sn-Ba-F structure) for fluoride-ion battery electrolyte

DFT_methodology.valence_e: Ba 5s2p6, Sn 5s2p2, F 2s2p5, Nd 5s2p6 (4f as core/semicore)
DFT_methodology.spin_polarization: NOT USED (paper claims 'Nd3+ has no open-shell d electrons' — questionable for 4f3)
DFT_methodology.DFT_plus_U: NOT USED (no Hubbard correction on Nd 4f)
DFT_methodology.AIMD: Γ-only k-point, used for diffusivity (Eq. 1-3) and thermal stability

references.Nd_doping_mechanism: Nd3+ (smaller, 1.81 Å vs Ba2+ 2.18 Å) replaces Ba2+ → Nd-F bond shorter (2.39 Å) and stronger (Nd-5p + F-2p hybridization) → distorts adjacent Ba-F polyhedron → Ba-F bond elongates (2.73-2.85 Å) → reduced Ba-F restriction → F-ion mobility increases.
references.structural_role: Nd doping induces structural reconstruction of Ba-F tetrahedron, increasing disorder degree of barium-fluoride coordination polyhedron. Nd-F-Ba bonding angle changes 123.81° → 173° at saddle point (vs BaSnF4 179.52°).
references.relevance_to_our_work: DIRECT precedent for Nd3+ doping in inorganic solid electrolyte at multiple concentrations (x=0.02 to 0.25). Validates: (1) using x=0.125 (~10% supercell) instead of experimental x=0.02 — pseudo-isolated defect model, (2) heterovalent doping with charge-compensating interstitial anions (F- in their case ↔ Li+ vacancies in our argyrodite case), (3) Nd induces local distortion that reduces ion-host coordination strength → mobility enhancement, (4) elastic property changes (Pugh ratio) follow trend of doping. KEY DIFFERENCE: their Nd substitutes Ba2+ (cation similar size), our Nd would substitute Li+ (cation similar charge for 2:1 ratio). Both treat 4f as quasi-core (no DFT+U, no spin polarization) — this is questionable for our work; we should use DFT+U (U=6 eV) + ISPIN=2 for proper 4f description.

methodology_critique.spin_polarization_missing: Nd3+ has 4f3 configuration with 3 unpaired electrons. Paper states 'Nd3+ has not open-shell d electrons' which conflates 4f and 5d. This is incorrect — 4f3 IS open-shell. Spin polarization should be ISPIN=2.
methodology_critique.DFT_plus_U_missing: PBE alone delocalizes 4f electrons → wrong band gap, wrong DOS positions of Nd 4f peaks. Paper reports band gap 3.41-3.69 eV but Nd 4f peak positions in DOS may be artifactual. Standard practice: DFT+U with U_eff=6 eV on Nd 4f (Loschen 2007, Topsakal 2014).
methodology_critique.consequence: Their reported electronic structure (band gap, DOS) may underestimate gap and misposition 4f peaks. Mechanical and structural results (lattice constants, bond lengths, formation energies, elastic constants, diffusion barriers via NEB) are likely reliable since they don't directly depend on 4f energy positions.
methodology_critique.salvaged_results: Trust: lattice/bonds/forces/elastic/NEB barriers/Bader (if reported). Distrust: band gap value/4f DOS position/electronic conductivity prediction.

useful_strategies_for_our_paper: 1. Multiple x values tested (0.02, 0.0625, 0.125, 0.25) — covers dilute to concentrated regime, justifies x=0.125-0.25 as 'best ductility/mobility balance'
2. Charge compensation handled automatically by adding/removing anion at interstitial — same approach we'll use for Li in argyrodite
3. Bond length redistribution analysis (Ba-F shortest vs Nd-F shortest) — direct analog to our planned Li-S vs Nd-S/O comparison
4. AIMD for thermal stability validation — we should adopt same approach (NVT 300K, 50-100 ps, monitor lattice/total energy)
5. Phase stability via convex hull (CPLAP) → competing phases search — adopt for Nd-doped argyrodite
6. Pugh ratio (B/G) and ductility narrative — strong story for paper if our argyrodite shows B/G change
7. NEB with charge-compensated vacancy — methodology directly applicable to Li migration in Nd-doped Li5.4 argyrodite
what_to_NOT_copy: 1. Skip 'no spin polarization' justification — for our 4f3 Nd we MUST use ISPIN=2
2. Skip 'no DFT+U' approach — we MUST use U_eff=6 eV on Nd 4f
3. Their conductivity number (5.35e-3 S/cm) is high but not directly comparable (different system, different chemistry)

Nd_concentration_decision_for_our_argyro.our_analog: x=0.20 (Li5.4-3xNdxLi vacancy in Model C 62-atom cell = 1 Nd) — comparable supercell size
Nd_concentration_decision_for_our_argyro.isolated_defect_validity: Their Nd-Nd distance ~5-7 Å in 49-atom supercell still gave clean results. Our Nd-Nd through periodic image >12 Å in 62-atom rhombo cell will be even safer.
Nd_concentration_decision_for_our_argyro.consistent_protocol: Single Nd in unit cell + ISPIN=2 + DFT+U(6 eV) → cleaner than Xiong's setup despite our smaller supercell

section_1_spin_states.their_argument: Nd ground state [Xe]4f^4 6s^2; Nd3+ is [Xe]4f^3 5s^2 5p^6. They claim 'Nd does not lose d electrons when transferred to Nd3+, so it is highly unlikely Nd has open-shell d electrons, therefore different spin states at Nd center are impossible.'
section_1_spin_states.critique: The argument confuses 4f vs 5d. Nd3+ 4f^3 IS open-shell (3 unpaired f electrons → S=3/2, L=6, ground term 4I_9/2). Their reasoning is flawed. They effectively treat 4f as core, which mishandles 4f electronic structure but may give acceptable results for non-electronic properties (lattice, elastic, Bader).
section_1_spin_states.their_refs_used: [1] Chen et al. JAP 2012 (NdFeO3 4f role); [2] Feng et al. Acta Mater 2011 (Ln2Zr2O7 pyrochlore); [3] Ban et al. JMMM 1998 (Mossbauer Nd valence)

section_3_F_interstitial_screening.method: For each x value (0.02, 0.0625, 0.125, 0.25), tested 6 candidate F-interstitial positions (F1-F6). Selected lowest-energy site.
section_3_F_interstitial_screening.implication_for_us: We need similar screening for Li-vacancy positions when doing Nd→Li substitution in argyrodite. With 27 Li sites, can sample top-N favorable vacancy locations using MLIP.

section_5_phase_competing.best_Nd_source: Nd5Sn3 (most negative formation energy, most favorable for synthesis)
section_5_phase_competing.Nd_NO3_3_alternative: Wide chemical potential range supports Nd(NO3)3 as feasible raw material
section_5_phase_competing.implication_for_us: Adopt similar convex-hull / phase competition analysis for Nd2O3 → argyrodite. Competing phases: Nd2S3, NdCl3, NdOCl, Li3Nd, LiNdO2, Nd2O3 itself.

section_7_thermal_stability_AIMD.Bader_invariance: Bader charges of Ba and Sn unchanged with Nd doping (Fig S23a) → no redox; framework stable

section_8_diffusion_paths.DOS_at_saddle: Nd-5p × F-2p hybridization stronger at saddle → energy lowering

section_13_electrochemical_decomp.Fig_S50_decomp_band_gaps: Ba0.875Nd0.125SnF4.125 ~3.5 eV; NdF3 wider; SnF2 wider; BaF2 widest — all passivating

figure_S15_analysis.trend: Non-monotonic. Lowest at intermediate x=0.02-0.0625, recovers at x=0.125, dips again at x=0.25
figure_S15_analysis.PDOS_decomposition: F-2p dominates valence band. Ba-5p deeper (-3 to -4 eV). Sn-5p near VBM. **Nd-5p shown but Nd-4f NOT projected** (cyan line nearly flat) — paper hides 4f either by treating as core or omitting projection.

figure_S29_analysis.key_mechanism: Saddle geometry asymmetry. Pristine BaSnF4 has SYMMETRIC saddle (linear Ba-F-Ba, both 2.47 Å) → both Ba atoms simultaneously increase hybridization with F → high simultaneous bond-breaking cost = 0.71 eV. Doped has ASYMMETRIC saddle (Nd-F=2.24, Ba-F=2.58 Å) → Nd-F barely hybridizes more (already short ionic bond) while Ba-F shortens but is weaker → distributed strain rather than peak strain → 0.18 eV barrier.
figure_S29_analysis.transferability_to_argyrodite: Same logic applies if Nd substitutes Li in argyrodite: Li-S/Cl bonds are weaker than Nd-S/Cl. Asymmetric saddle in Li migration through Nd-modified site should give lower barrier. Conceptually: Nd 'pre-stretches' one side of the migration channel by anchoring strongly.

figure_S30_S31_analysis.S30_pristine_BaSnF4: Both Ba1-F and F-Ba2 bonds show strong increase in hybridization at saddle (2.47 Å). Both bonds simultaneously become more covalent. F-2p × Ba-5p overlap intensifies symmetrically. High concurrent bond-strengthening = high barrier.

S31_doped_system.Nd_F_bond: DOS at initial (2.36 Å), saddle (2.24 Å), final (2.36 Å) — minimal hybridization change. Nd-5p contribution (cyan) tiny; Nd-F is largely IONIC, not covalent. Saddle compression doesn't trigger strong covalent bonding.
S31_doped_system.Ba_F_bond: F-Ba2 (2.77 Å initial → 2.58 Å saddle → 2.77 Å final). Some hybridization increase at saddle, but smaller in absolute magnitude than pristine BaSnF4.

figure_S30_S31_analysis.publication_template: These DOS plots are the GOLD STANDARD for explaining ion migration barriers via electronic structure. Format: 3 stacked panels (initial/saddle/final), 2 elements (host atom + migrating ion), with bond length annotated for each. Use this exact format for our Li migration NEB in Nd-doped argyrodite.
what_to_extract_for_paper: 1. Initial → saddle bond length compression (Δd in Å)
2. DOS overlap area change (proxy for hybridization, integrate near EF)

figure_S23_analysis.interpretation: Nd doping does NOT trigger redox of host framework atoms. Ba and Sn maintain their +2 ionicity. Only Nd-F bond locally formed; rest of crystal electronically unchanged.
figure_S23_analysis.DOS_panel_b: BaSnF4 vs Ba0.875Nd0.125SnF4.125 nearly indistinguishable. VB structure preserved. CB shifts negligible.
figure_S23_analysis.implication_for_us: Adopt SAME figure structure: (a) Bader of Li/P/S/Cl vs Nd concentration → show framework charge invariance; (b) Total DOS comparison undoped vs doped → show electronic structure preserved EXCEPT for new 4f peak. The CONTRAST against Xiong's missing 4f is our methodological highlight.
